docs.title: Pixtheme documentation
docs.text:
Setup guides for Pixtheme themes and modules on the HubSpot CMS.

  • Event Time

    A complete website for conferences, summits, webinars and meetups.

    Read the docs →

  • Openhouse

    A real estate website with HubDB listings, agents, neighborhoods and lead forms.

    Read the docs →

  • Smart Comparison Table

    A free module for comparing pricing plans or products side by side.

    Read the docs →

Need help? Email support@pixtheme.com.

docs.title: Welcome to Event Time
docs.text:
Event Time is a HubSpot CMS theme for event websites. It gives you everything from the first "save the date" page to the thank-you page after registration.

Live demo: pixtheme.com/event-time-demo

docs.title: What's included
docs.text: Home pages 5 layouts: dark conference, centered keynote, light corporate summit, webinar, meetup Event pages About, Speakers, Schedule, Tickets, Venue, Sponsors, Contact, Coming soon, Registration thank you Blog Blog listing and blog post templates System pages 404, 500, password prompt, search results, email subscription pages and membership pages Modules 22 drag-and-drop modules plus the site header and footer Sections 10 ready-made sections you can drop into any page

docs.title: Where to start
docs.text:
• Install the theme
  • Build your event site
  • Section style and the Style tab

docs.title: Requirements
docs.text:
• A HubSpot account that can create website pages. Event Time works with website pages, landing pages and the HubSpot blog. Membership pages need a Content Hub plan that includes memberships.
  • No coding is needed. Everything is edited in the HubSpot page editor and theme settings.

docs.title: Highlighted words
docs.text: Headings can show one or more words in your brand gradient, like "Where bold ideas meet the people who build them".

docs.title: How to highlight words
docs.text:
Wrap the words in asterisks inside the heading field:

Where *bold ideas* meet the people who build them

The asterisks aren't shown on the page. You can highlight more than one part:

Keynotes, *workshops* and *panels*

docs.title: Older "Highlighted words" field
docs.text: Some modules also have a Highlighted words (optional) field. It's still supported: type the exact words from the heading there. If the heading contains asterisks, the asterisks win and this field is ignored.

docs.title: Change the highlight color
docs.text: By default highlighted words use the brand gradient. To change it for one section, open the module's Style tab › Custom styles › Text colors › Highlighted words.

docs.title: Ready-made sections
docs.text:
Sections are pre-built blocks with demo content that you can drop into any page made with a drag-and-drop template.

In the page editor, click + (Add) › Sections, then look for:

Section Contains Event hero Opening section with heading, date, location, buttons and countdown About with video Intro text, highlights, key numbers and a video in a lightbox Schedule tabs Agenda with one tab per day Speakers Speaker grid Countdown Large countdown with a button Ticket pricing Three ticket cards with a highlighted plan Testimonials Attendee quotes FAQ Questions and answers Call to action banner Bold banner with two buttons Newsletter Signup form

You can also save your own edited sections: hover over a section in the editor, click Save section and reuse it on other pages.

docs.title: Section style and the Style tab
docs.text: Every Event Time module has a Style tab in the page editor. Use it to make one section look different from the rest of the page. Empty fields keep the theme design, so you only set what you want to change.

docs.title: Section style
docs.text:
The quickest way to change a section. Choose one of:

Option Result Same as the page Follows the page's dark or light scheme (default) Dark Dark section, even on a light page Light Light section, even on a dark page Tinted background A softly colored background to separate the section Brand gradient Full brand-gradient background with white text, great for call-to-action sections

Tip

Alternate Same as the page and Tinted background down a long page to give it rhythm without changing any colors.

docs.title: Custom styles
docs.text:
For full control, open Custom styles:

Group Settings Spacing Space above and below the section, on desktop and on mobile Background Background color, background image, image overlay color and image position Text colors Headings, body text, secondary text, small labels, highlighted words and links Cards Card background, card border and card corner radius Buttons and accents Gradient start and gradient end colors for this section's buttons and highlights Hover and active states Button hover background and text, link hover color, card hover border and background, active background and text (for example the selected day tab or an open FAQ question)

Custom styles work on top of the section style. For example, choose Light and then set a custom card background.

Note

The Testimonials module has its own, larger Styles tab with layout-specific options.

docs.title: Theme settings
docs.text: Theme settings change the whole site at once. Open any Event Time page in the editor, click the Theme icon in the left sidebar, then Edit theme settings.

docs.title: Brand
docs.text: Setting What it does Primary color Main brand color, used for buttons, highlights and the start of the gradient. Secondary color Second brand color, used for accents. Heading font Font for headings. Default: Titillium Web. Body font Font for text. Default: DM Sans.

docs.title: Colors
docs.text:
Setting What it does Color scheme Dark or Light. This is the default for all pages. The three light home templates are always light. Page background, Card background, Raised card background, Border color, Muted text color, Link color Colors for the dark scheme. Gradient end color The second color of the brand gradient used on buttons and highlights.

Light scheme colors has the same settings for light pages, plus heading, text and accent text colors.

docs.title: Buttons
docs.text: Setting Default Use gradient on primary buttons On. Turn it off for solid primary-color buttons. Corner radius 999 (fully rounded). Use 0–8 for square buttons. Vertical padding / Horizontal padding 15 / 32 px Text style Uppercase or Normal

docs.title: Layout
docs.text: Setting Default Maximum content width 1240 px Section spacing on desktop 110 px Section spacing on mobile 72 px Card corner radius 16 px

docs.title: Header
docs.text:
• Transparent header at the top of the page (on by default)
  • Sticky header (on by default)
  • Header background when scrolled, menu link color and menu link hover color, for dark and light pages

docs.title: Blog
docs.text: Turn blog features on or off: topic filter, reading time, author on post cards, share buttons, topics under posts, author box, related posts, subscribe form on the listing and the ticket banner under posts.

docs.title: Footer
docs.text:
Footer background, heading color, text color and link hover color.

Note

To change just one section instead of the whole site, use that section's Style tab. See Section style and the Style tab.

docs.title: Recommended pages
docs.text:
A typical event site uses these templates. Create the pages you need and skip the rest.

Page Template to choose Home One of the 5 home templates (see below) Speakers Speakers Schedule Schedule Tickets Tickets Venue Venue Sponsors Sponsors About About Contact Contact Registration thank you Registration thank you Coming soon / waitlist Coming soon (use it before tickets go on sale)

docs.title: Choose a home page
docs.text: Template Best for Home Dark conference site with countdown, agenda, tickets and blog posts Home (centered hero) Keynote-style layout with a centered heading and countdown Home (corporate summit, light) Light, corporate B2B summit with a photo hero Home (webinar or virtual event, light) Registration page for a webinar or online event Home (meetup or workshop, light) Small meetups and workshops with an RSVP form

docs.title: Create a page
docs.text:
1. Go to Content › Website Pages and click Create › Website page.
  2. Choose Event Time and pick a template.
  3. Give the page a name, then replace the demo text and images. Every section is a module: click it to edit it in the left sidebar.
  4. Set the page URL, title and meta description in Settings.
  5. Click Publish when you're ready.

Tip

Every template comes filled with realistic demo content, so you can see how each section is meant to look. Edit the text rather than starting from an empty page.

docs.title: Add, move and remove sections
docs.text:
• Add a module or section: click + (Add) in the left sidebar, find it by name (for example "Schedule Tabs") and drag it onto the page.
  • Move a section: drag it by its handle in the page editor.
  • Remove a section: hover over it and click the delete icon.

docs.title: Link your pages together
docs.text:
1. Create a navigation menu in Settings › Content › Navigation menus with your new pages.
  2. Choose that menu in the site header (see Header and footer).
  3. Update the button links in each page (for example "Get your ticket" should point to your Tickets page).

docs.title: Before you publish
docs.text:
• Set the event date in every countdown (hero, countdown and coming soon modules)
  • Choose your HubSpot forms (see Forms and the registration flow)
  • Replace the demo speaker photos, logos and gallery images
  • Check the header menu and footer links
  • Preview on mobile with the device switcher in the page editor

docs.title: Forms and the registration flow
docs.text: Event Time uses your own HubSpot forms, so every registration, waitlist signup and question lands in your HubSpot contacts.

docs.title: Modules with a form
docs.text:
Module Typical form Coming soon Waitlist signup (email only) Contact form Contact, speaker application or sponsor enquiry Newsletter signup Newsletter or "get updates" form

Choose the form in the module's Form field. Create forms in Marketing › Forms.

docs.title: A complete registration flow
docs.text:
1. Before tickets go on sale: publish the Coming soon page with a waitlist form and a countdown to the sale date.
  2. Tickets: link the buttons in the Pricing tickets module to your ticket provider, a registration form page or a HubSpot payment link.
  3. After registration: in the form's settings in HubSpot, set What should happen after a visitor submits this form? to Redirect to another page and choose your Registration thank you page.
  4. Thank-you page: set the event details and the Add to calendar start and end times so visitors can save the event to Google Calendar, Apple Calendar or Outlook.

Note

Forms take their look from the theme automatically. You don't need to style them in the form editor.

docs.title: Countdowns
docs.text:
The hero, countdown and coming soon modules have an Event start date and time field. Pick the date and time in the date picker. When the countdown reaches zero, it shows the Text after the countdown ends instead (for example "The event is live").

Warning

Each countdown has its own date. If your event date changes, update it in every module that shows a countdown.

docs.title: Header and footer
docs.text:
The header and footer are global: you edit them once and the change appears on every Event Time page.

To edit them, open any Event Time page in the editor, click the header or footer, then click Open global content editor.

docs.title: Header
docs.text: Setting What it does Logo Your logo. Use a light version, because the default header is dark. Logo height Height of the logo in pixels. Logo on light pages A dark version of your logo, used on the light home templates. Logo link Where the logo links to, usually your home page. Menu The navigation menu to show. Create menus in Settings › Content › Navigation menus. Menu levels How many dropdown levels to show. Language switcher Shows a language menu when the page has translations (see below). Header button The button on the right, for example "Get tickets". Top bar An optional thin bar above the header with the event date, email, phone and social links. Labels and screen reader text Text for the mobile menu buttons and skip link. Translate these if your site isn't in English.

docs.title: Language switcher
docs.text:
If your site is in more than one language, the header shows a language menu with a globe icon. It lists the current language and every published translation of the page, and takes visitors to the same page in the language they choose.

  1. Create a translation of a page: open the page in the editor and choose File › New › Multi-language variation.
  2. Publish the translation. The switcher appears automatically on both versions.

Pages without translations don't show the switcher. To hide it everywhere, turn off Show language switcher in the header's Language switcher settings. Translate Button text for screen readers if your site isn't in English.

The header is transparent at the top of the page and sticky while scrolling. You can change both in Theme settings › Header.

docs.title: Footer
docs.text:
Setting What it does Brand Footer logo, logo link, a short about text and social links. Link column 1 and Link column 2 A heading and a navigation menu for each column. Contact column Address, email and phone number. Bottom bar Copyright text and an optional legal links menu (privacy policy, terms).

Footer colors are in Theme settings › Footer.

Warning

If a footer column is empty on your site, it's because no menu is selected for it yet. Choose a menu in Link column 1 and Link column 2.

docs.title: 1. Get the theme
docs.text:
1. Open the HubSpot Template Marketplace and search for Event Time.
  2. Click Get (or Buy) and choose your HubSpot account.
  3. HubSpot adds the theme to Content › Design Manager under @marketplace. You don't need to download anything.

docs.title: 2. Set it as your active theme (optional)
docs.text:
If Event Time will power your whole website:

  1. Open the Themes page in HubSpot (type "Themes" in the HubSpot search bar to find it).
  2. Find Event Time and click Set as active theme.

You can also use Event Time for one event site next to your existing theme. Just pick an Event Time template when you create a page.

docs.title: 3. Set your brand
docs.text:
Before building pages, open Edit theme settings and set:

  • Primary color and Secondary color (your brand colors; they make the gradient)
  • Heading font and Body font
  • Color scheme: Dark or Light

See Theme settings for every option.

Note

To open theme settings, edit any Event Time page, click the Theme icon in the left sidebar of the page editor, then Edit theme settings.

docs.title: 4. Next step
docs.text: Create your pages: Build your event site.

First release.

  • 5 home page templates and 9 event page templates
  • Blog listing and blog post templates
  • 11 system page templates
  • 22 modules plus the site header and footer
  • 10 ready-made sections
  • Section style and Custom styles on every module, including hover and active states
  • Dark and light color schemes
  • Language switcher in the header for multi-language sites

docs.title: FAQ and troubleshooting
docs.text:
How do I switch the whole site between dark and light?

Open Theme settings › Colors › Color scheme and choose Dark or Light. The three light home templates (summit, webinar and meetup) stay light either way.

How do I make just one section light on a dark page (or the other way round)?

Click the section, open its Style tab and set Section style to Light or Dark. See Section style and the Style tab.

The countdown shows zeros or the "ended" text.

The date in Event start date and time is in the past. Set a future date in the module. Each countdown has its own date.

My footer columns are empty.

Choose a navigation menu for Link column 1 and Link column 2 in the global footer. See Header and footer.

My logo is hard to see.

The dark pages need a light (white) logo. Set a dark version in the header's Logo on light pages field for the light templates.

The video in "About with video" doesn't play.

Use a normal YouTube or Vimeo page URL, for example https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=... or https://vimeo.com/123456789. Private videos and videos with embedding turned off can't play on other sites.

The map shows the wrong place.

Make Map search more specific: add the city and country, or use the full street address.

How do I highlight words in a heading?

Wrap them in asterisks: Where *bold ideas* meet. See Highlighted words.

Can I use Event Time for more than one event?

Yes. Create a separate set of pages for each event (for example under /2027/ and /2028/), or clone your pages and update the content.

Can I edit the theme code?

Marketplace themes can't be edited directly. To change code, clone the theme in Content › Design Manager. A cloned theme doesn't receive updates from the marketplace.

docs.title: Support
docs.text:
We're happy to help with setup questions and anything that doesn't work as described.

Email: support@pixtheme.com

Please include:

  • A link to the page with the problem
  • What you expected to happen and what happened instead
  • A screenshot, if it helps

Support is in English.

docs.title: All modules
docs.text:
Find any module in the page editor's Add panel by searching for its name. Each module has a Content tab for text and images and a Style tab (see Section style and the Style tab).

Module What it's for Details Hero Opening section with event name, date, location, buttons and countdown Hero Page intro Opening section for inner pages, with breadcrumbs Page intro Coming soon Full-screen teaser with countdown and waitlist form Coming soon Schedule tabs Agenda with one tab per day Schedule tabs Countdown Large countdown with a button Countdown Marquee strip Endless scrolling band of large text Marquee strip Speakers Speaker grid with photos and social links Speakers Testimonials Quotes in 5 layouts with ratings and video Testimonials About with video Intro, highlights, key numbers and a video About with video Photo gallery Photo grid or mosaic with a full-screen viewer Photo gallery Pricing tickets Ticket cards with a highlighted plan Pricing tickets Sponsor tiers Sponsor logos grouped by level Sponsor tiers Logo strip Logos as a grid or a scrolling strip Logo strip Venue map Address, Google map, directions and travel tips Venue map Info cards Cards with an icon or photo, for hotels, perks or features Info cards FAQ Questions and answers in an accordion FAQ Contact form HubSpot form next to contact details Contact form Newsletter signup Signup with a HubSpot form Newsletter signup Call to action banner Bold banner with two buttons Call to action banner Recent posts Latest blog posts as cards Recent posts Thank you Registration confirmation with add-to-calendar buttons Thank you Error page Message for the 404 and 500 pages Error page

The Site header and Site footer are covered in Header and footer.

docs.title: Fields many modules share
docs.text:
• Section heading: eyebrow text (small label above), heading, heading level (H1, H2 or H3), intro text and alignment (left or center). Use only one H1 per page, usually in the hero or page intro.
  • Buttons: text, link and style (Primary (gradient), Outline or White). A button with empty text is hidden.
  • Anchor ID: lets you link to the section, for example #schedule. Use it for "View schedule" buttons on the same page.
  • Labels: small texts for screen readers and buttons. Translate them if your site isn't in English.

docs.title: Contact form
docs.text:
A HubSpot form in a card, next to contact details.

Field Notes Section heading Contact details Icon, title, text and an optional link (for example a mailto: link). Social links Heading, network and profile URL. Form card Heading, text and the HubSpot form.

Use it for contact, speaker applications, sponsor enquiries or meetup RSVPs.

docs.title: Newsletter signup
docs.text:
A simple signup section.

Field Notes Eyebrow text, Heading, Text Form A HubSpot form, usually with just an email field.

docs.title: Call to action banner
docs.text:
A bold banner, for example "Become a sponsor" or "Tickets are selling fast".

Field Notes Eyebrow text, Heading, Text Primary button, Secondary button Background Brand gradient, Image or Card color. Background image Used when the background is Image.

docs.title: Recent posts
docs.text:
Your latest blog posts as cards.

Field Notes Blog Which HubSpot blog to show. Number of posts Show author, Show date, Show excerpt Read more text View all button Usually links to your blog listing.

docs.title: Hero, page intro and coming soon
Hero
docs.text:
The large opening section of a home page.

Field Notes Eyebrow text, Heading, Intro text Mark words in the heading with *asterisks* to highlight them. Event details Date and location, shown with icons. Primary button, Secondary button For example "Get your ticket" and "View schedule". Countdown card Show a countdown card with a title and the event start date and time. Background Background image, overlay darkness and glowing shapes. Layout Text left, countdown card right, Centered, countdown below or Text left, photo right. Side photo The photo for the Text left, photo right layout.

docs.title: Page intro
docs.text:
The opening section of inner pages (Speakers, Schedule, Tickets and so on).

Field Notes Breadcrumbs Show or hide, home link text and link, and the current page text. Eyebrow text, Heading, Intro text Event details Optional date and location. Primary button, Secondary button Optional. Alignment Center or left. Height Compact or Tall. Background Background image, overlay darkness and glowing shapes.

docs.title: Coming soon
docs.text:
A full-screen teaser for before tickets go on sale. Used on the Coming soon page and the webinar home page.

Field Notes Eyebrow text, Heading, Text Event details Date and location. Countdown Show a countdown, the date and time to count down to, and the labels. Waitlist perks A short list with icons, for example "Early-bird prices". Form card Heading, text, the HubSpot form and small print (for example your privacy note). Social links Network and profile URL. Background Background image, overlay darkness and glowing shapes.

docs.title: Speakers
docs.text:
A grid of speaker cards.

Field Notes Speakers Photo, name, job title, company, LinkedIn URL, X (Twitter) URL and an optional profile page link. Speakers per row on desktop Usually 4. Phones show fewer automatically. Button below the speakers For example "See all speakers".

Note

Use square photos of the same size (at least 600 × 600 px) so all cards line up.

docs.title: Testimonials
docs.text:
Attendee or customer quotes with five layouts.

Field Notes Testimonials Quote, author name, job title, company, photo, company logo, star rating, review date, review source and an optional video testimonial. Turn on Feature this testimonial to make one stand out. Layout Carousel, Grid, Masonry wall, Featured spotlight or Simple list, with columns for desktop, tablet and mobile, carousel options and quote length. Structured data Optionally adds review data (JSON-LD) for search engines. Only use it for genuine reviews. Styles tab Colors, card style, ratings and more, separate from the other modules.

Video testimonials load only when a visitor clicks play, so they don't slow the page down.

docs.title: About with video
docs.text:
An event introduction with a video.

Field Notes Section heading Highlights Short title and text pairs, for example "60+ speakers". Button Optional. Video Thumbnail image and a YouTube or Vimeo URL. The video opens in a lightbox. A badge number and text can sit on the thumbnail, for example "8th edition". Key numbers Number and label pairs, for example "1,200 attendees".

YouTube videos load from the privacy-friendly youtube-nocookie.com domain.

docs.title: Photo gallery
docs.text:
A photo grid with a full-screen viewer.

Field Notes Layout Mosaic (first photo large) or Even grid. Photos per row on desktop Photos Photo and optional caption. Open photos in a full-screen viewer Visitors can click through the photos with arrows or the keyboard. Button below the gallery Optional.

docs.title: Schedule tabs
docs.text:
The event agenda, with one tab per day.

Field Notes Section heading Eyebrow, heading, intro and alignment. Days Add one item per day: Tab label (for example "Day 01") and Date. Sessions (inside each day) Time, session title, description, speakers, room or location and session type. Session type Keynote, Workshop, Panel, Networking or Break. Each type is shown as a badge on the session card. Layout Cards or Timeline. Button below the schedule Optional, for example "Download the full agenda". Labels The badge names and the speaker prefix. Translate them if needed.

Note

A one-day event? Add just one day. The tabs are hidden when there's only one.

docs.title: Countdown
docs.text:
A large countdown to the event start, with a button.

Field Notes Eyebrow text, Heading Event start date and time The moment the countdown counts down to. Countdown labels Days, hours, minutes, seconds, and the text to show after the countdown ends. Button For example "Get your ticket". Background image Optional.

docs.title: Marquee strip
docs.text:
An endless scrolling band of large text, for example "60+ speakers ✦ Lisbon, Portugal ✦ February 24–25". Place it between sections.

Field Notes Items One text per item. Style Gradient band, Outlined text or Dark band. Seconds per loop Higher is slower. Direction Right to left or left to right. Tilt the band Slightly rotates the band for a bolder look.

Visitors can pause the animation with the pause button, and it doesn't move for visitors who turned on "reduce motion" on their device.

docs.title: Thank you
docs.text:
The confirmation after someone registers. Set your registration form to redirect to the page that uses this module (see Forms and the registration flow).

Field Notes Eyebrow text, Heading, Text For example "See you in Lisbon!" Ticket card Event name, ticket type, date, time, location and small print, shown as a ticket. Add to calendar Event title, start, end, location and description. Adds a Google Calendar button and a calendar file button for Apple Calendar and Outlook. Next steps Heading and a list of title and text pairs, for example "Check your inbox". Primary button, Secondary button Share Share links with a page to share and a message, so attendees can invite colleagues. Show confetti A short confetti burst when the page opens. It's skipped for visitors who prefer reduced motion.

docs.title: Error page
docs.text:
Used on the 404 and 500 system pages.

Field Notes Error code Shown large, for example "404". Eyebrow text, Heading, Text Primary button, Secondary button For example "Back to home" and "View schedule". Site search Show a search field, its placeholder, button text and the search results page path. Helpful links Heading plus link text and links to your main pages.

docs.title: Pricing tickets
docs.text:
Ticket or package cards.

Field Notes Plans Plan name, currency symbol, price, price note (for example "/ person"), short description, features and a button. Features Each feature can be marked as included or not included. Highlight this plan Makes the card stand out. Add Badge text such as "Most popular".

Note

The button can link anywhere: your ticketing provider, a HubSpot payment link or a registration form page.

docs.title: Sponsor tiers
docs.text:
Sponsor logos grouped by level.

Field Notes Sponsor levels Level name (for example "Platinum"), short description, logo size (Large, Medium or Small), highlight this level, and the logos with links. Logo style Single color (white on dark, dark on light) or Original colors. Call to action card An optional card at the end, for example "Become a sponsor", with two buttons.

docs.title: Logo strip
docs.text:
Partner, sponsor or organizer logos.

Field Notes Heading For example "Trusted by teams at". Layout Grid or Endless scroll. Logos per row on desktop For the grid layout. Logos Logo and optional link. Logo style Single color or Original colors.

Tip

Single color works best with transparent PNG or SVG logos. It makes logos from different brands look consistent.

docs.title: Venue map
docs.text:
Venue details with an embedded Google map.

Field Notes Venue name, Address Shown in a card next to the map. Map search What the map searches for, for example "Lisbon Congress Center". Use the venue name plus city, or the full address. Map zoom Higher numbers zoom in closer. Dark map colors Darkens the map to match dark pages. Directions button text Opens Google Maps directions to the venue. Travel tips Icon, title and text, for example "From the airport". Map position on desktop Right or left.

No Google API key is needed.

docs.title: Info cards
docs.text:
Flexible cards for hotels, perks, benefits or features.

Field Notes Cards Photo or icon, badge, small detail line, title, text, link text and link. Cards per row on desktop Section background Page background or Tinted band.

Examples from the demo: partner hotels with photos and "Book a room" links, travel tips with icons, sponsor benefits.

docs.title: FAQ
docs.text:
Questions and answers in an accessible accordion.

Field Notes Questions Question and answer (the answer can contain links and formatting). Open the first question Allow only one open answer at a time Help card An optional card next to the questions, for example "Still have questions?" with a button.

docs.title: Blog
docs.text:
Event Time includes two blog templates:

  • Blog listing: post cards with an optional topic filter, subscribe form and a call-to-action banner
  • Blog post: the post with reading time, share buttons, topics, author box, related posts and a ticket banner

docs.title: Use them for your blog
docs.text:
1. Go to Settings › Content › Blog and choose your blog.
  2. Open Templates and choose Blog listing for the listing page and Blog post for posts.
  3. Save.

docs.title: Turn features on or off
docs.text:
All blog options are in Theme settings › Blog:

Setting Default Show topic filter on the blog listing On Show reading time On Show author on post cards On Show share buttons on posts On Show topics under posts On Show author box under posts On Show related posts On Show subscribe form on the blog listing On Show ticket banner under blog posts On

docs.title: Show recent posts on other pages
docs.text: Add the Recent posts module to any page (the dark Home template already has it) and choose which blog to show.

docs.title: Page templates
docs.text: Event Time has 14 page templates. Each one is a drag-and-drop page filled with demo content, so you can edit, move, add or remove any section.

docs.title: Home pages
docs.text: Template Scheme Sections Home Dark Hero with countdown card, logo strip, about with video, marquee, schedule, countdown, speakers, call to action, ticket pricing, testimonials, FAQ, newsletter, recent blog posts Home (centered hero) Dark Centered hero, logo strip, speakers, marquee, about with video, schedule, gallery, sponsors, ticket pricing, venue map, FAQ, call to action Home (corporate summit, light) Light Hero with side photo, logo strip, about with video, speakers, schedule, ticket pricing, testimonials, FAQ, call to action Home (webinar or virtual event, light) Light Registration hero with countdown and form, info cards, speakers, agenda, FAQ, call to action Home (meetup or workshop, light) Light Hero, info cards, agenda, speakers, RSVP form, venue map, newsletter

docs.title: Event pages
docs.text:
Template Sections Speakers Page intro, speakers, call to action, newsletter Schedule Page intro, schedule tabs, countdown, speakers, newsletter Tickets Page intro, ticket pricing, marquee, FAQ, call to action Venue Page intro, venue map, travel info cards, gallery, hotel cards, FAQ, call to action Sponsors Page intro, sponsor tiers, benefit cards, sponsorship packages, contact form About Page intro, about with video, marquee, gallery, logo strip, testimonials, call to action Contact Page intro, contact form, venue map, FAQ Coming soon Full-screen teaser with countdown and waitlist form, logo strip Registration thank you Confirmation with ticket card and add-to-calendar buttons, next-step cards, FAQ

Note

The Coming soon page has a logo-only header and a slim footer, so visitors focus on the waitlist form. Its logo is set on the page itself, not in the global header. Keep the Coming soon and Registration thank you pages out of your navigation menu.

docs.title: System pages
docs.text:
System pages are pages HubSpot shows automatically, such as "page not found". Event Time styles all of them so they match your site.

Template Used for 404 Page not found Missing pages 500 Server error Server errors Password prompt Password-protected pages Search results Site search Email subscription preferences Email preference center Email subscriptions confirmation After someone updates their email preferences Email backup unsubscribe Backup unsubscribe page Membership login Private content login Membership registration Private content registration Membership reset password request Forgotten password Membership reset password Setting a new password

docs.title: Turn them on
docs.text:
1. Go to Settings › Content › Pages and open the System pages tab.
  2. For each page, choose the matching Event Time template.
  3. Save.

Email subscription pages are set in Settings › Marketing › Email › Subscriptions. Membership pages are set in Settings › Content › Private content (they need a plan that includes memberships).

The 404 and 500 pages use the Error page module, with a message, two buttons, site search and helpful links. The default text works for any event site.

Note

System page text is set in the template. To change it, clone the template in Content › Design Manager (right-click › Clone), edit the module values in the clone, then choose the clone as your system page.

docs.title: Welcome to Openhouse
docs.text:
Openhouse is a HubSpot CMS theme for real estate agents and agencies. It turns your listings, agents and neighborhoods into a clean, light website, and sends every inquiry and valuation request straight into your HubSpot CRM.

Live demo: assets.pixtheme.com/openhouse-demo

docs.title: What's included
docs.text: Home pages 5 designs: agency, single agent, luxury, commercial and new development Property pages Listings with search, filters and sorting, and a page for every property with gallery, floor plan, video, map, mortgage calculator and inquiry form Team and areas Agents list with profile pages, neighborhoods list with area guides Company pages Sell your home (valuation request), About, Contact Blog Blog listing and blog post templates System pages 404, 500, password prompt, search results, email subscription pages and membership pages Modules 24 drag-and-drop modules plus the site header and footer Sections 12 ready-made sections you can drop into any page

docs.title: Where to start
docs.text:
• Install the theme
  • Set up your listings (HubDB)
  • Build your site
  • Forms and leads

docs.title: Requirements
docs.text:
• A HubSpot account that can create website pages.
  • Property, agent and neighborhood pages from HubDB (one page per row, created automatically) need Content Hub Professional or Enterprise.
  • On Content Hub Starter you can still use every page: the Property Cards, Agent Cards and Neighborhood Tiles modules let you type the content in, and the Property Details module works on a normal page.
  • Membership pages need a Content Hub plan that includes memberships.
  • No coding is needed. Everything is edited in the page editor, theme settings and HubDB.

No MLS or IDX feed

Openhouse doesn't connect to an MLS or IDX feed. You add properties in HubDB, which is a spreadsheet-like table in HubSpot. If you'd like your listings synced from another system, contact us about a custom integration.

docs.title: Ready-made sections
docs.text:
Sections are pre-built blocks you can add to any Openhouse page. In the page editor, click + Add, open Sections, and drag one onto the page. Then edit it like any other module.

Section What it is Hero with property search Large photo hero with a search bar for location, type and price Featured properties Property cards with photo, price, status badge and key facts Services Cards for buying, selling, renting or any service you offer Image and text Photo with a stat card next to text, a checklist and buttons Neighborhoods Photo tiles for the areas you cover Agents Team cards with photo, role, phone and email Client reviews Star ratings and quotes from buyers and sellers How it works Numbered steps, for example how selling with you works Valuation form Text with a checklist next to a HubSpot form Mortgage calculator Monthly payment calculator with price, down payment, rate and term FAQ Accordion of questions and answers Call to action banner Dark banner with a photo, a heading and two buttons

docs.title: Section style and the Style tab
docs.text: Every Openhouse content module has a Style tab in the page editor. Use it to make one section look different from the rest of the page. Empty fields keep the theme design, so you only set what you want to change.

docs.title: Section style
docs.text:
Option Result Same as the page Uses the page background (default) Light White background Soft (warm background) The soft, warm background from theme settings, to separate sections Dark Dark background with light text, great for calls to action

Tip

Alternate Same as the page and Soft down a long page to give it rhythm without changing any colors.

docs.title: Custom styles
docs.text:
For full control, open Custom styles:

Group Settings Spacing Space above and below the section, on desktop and on mobile Background Background color, background image, image overlay color and image position Text colors Headings, body text, secondary text, small labels, highlighted words and links Cards Card background, card border and card corner radius Buttons and accents Primary button color, text and hover color, accent color, card hover border

docs.title: Highlighted words
docs.text:
Wrap words in a heading in *asterisks* to show them in the highlight style (italic, in your primary color):

Find a home you'll *love* in San Francisco

On dark sections, highlighted words use the accent color.

docs.title: Theme settings
docs.text:
Open theme settings from any Openhouse page: click the Theme icon in the left sidebar of the page editor, then Edit theme settings. Changes apply to every page.

Group Settings Brand Primary color, accent color, heading font, body font Colors Page background, soft section background, card background, border color, muted text, link color, dark section background, text on dark sections Buttons Corner radius, vertical and horizontal padding, text style Layout Maximum content width, section spacing on desktop and mobile, card corner radius, soft shadows on cards, fade sections in on scroll Property listings Currency, currency position, thousands separator, area unit Header Sticky header, header background, menu link colors, line under the header Blog Topic buttons, subscribe form, reading time, author on cards, share buttons, topics under posts, author box, related posts Footer Footer background, heading color, text color, link hover color

Fonts

Openhouse looks best with a serif for headings (the demo uses Fraunces) and a clean sans-serif for text (Inter). For a more modern look, try a sans-serif for both.

docs.title: Build your site
docs.text: Create each page with Content › Website pages › Create, choose the Openhouse template, then edit the text and photos in the page editor. The demo content is already in place, so every page looks finished from the start.

docs.title: Recommended pages
docs.text: Page Template Suggested address Home Home (or one of the other home designs) / Listings and property pages Property listings and property pages /listings Agents and profiles Agents and agent profiles /agents Neighborhoods and guides Neighborhoods and neighborhood guides /neighborhoods Sell your home Sell your home /sell About About /about Contact Contact /contact

docs.title: Connect the HubDB pages
docs.text:
The listings, agents and neighborhoods templates each make two kinds of page from one page: the list (for example all properties) and a page for every row (each property).

  1. Create the page with the template, for example Property listings and property pages.
  2. Open Settings › Advanced › Dynamic pages and choose your table as the data source, for example Properties.
  3. In the editor, click the Property Listings module and choose your table under Properties table. Set Property pages to this page's address, for example /listings.
  4. Click the Property Details module and choose your Agents table, so each property shows its agent.
  5. Publish. Your list is at /listings and each property at /listings/{page path}.

Do the same for Agents (data source: your Agents table) and Neighborhoods (data source: your Neighborhoods table).

Why the editor shows every module

The editor shows the list modules and the detail modules together, so you can edit both in one place. Visitors only see the list on /listings, and only the property modules on a property page.

docs.title: Point the other modules to your tables
docs.text:
These modules can also read your tables. Open each one and choose the table:

Module Setting Agent Cards Source: My agents table (HubDB), then the table and Agent profile pages Neighborhood Tiles Source: My neighborhoods table (HubDB), the table, Neighborhood guide pages, and optionally the Properties table for the counts Home Hero search bar Listings page: your listings page address

The home pages show homes with the Property Cards module, where you type each home in. To show your HubDB homes instead, replace it with the Property Listings module, set What to show to Featured properties only, and choose your table and property pages. Tick featured on the homes you want there.

docs.title: Content Hub Starter
docs.text:
Without dynamic pages, build the same site with typed-in content:

  • Use Property Cards instead of Property Listings to show homes.
  • Create one page per property with the Property listings and property pages template and fill in Property (when the page is not connected to HubDB) in the Property Details module. Hide the Property Listings module on those pages.
  • Set Agent Cards and Neighborhood Tiles to Typed in below.

docs.title: The other home designs
docs.text:
Template Best for Home Agencies with a team and many listings Home – single agent One agent's personal site, with a portrait hero and their own listings Home – luxury High-end homes, with a full-screen photo hero Home – commercial Offices and retail, with a contact form for leasing enquiries Home – new development One project, with gallery, unit types, availability table and register-interest form

Next: Header, footer and menus.

docs.title: Forms and leads
docs.text: Openhouse uses your own HubSpot forms, so every inquiry, valuation request and contact message creates or updates a contact in your CRM. You choose the form in each module.

docs.title: Where the forms are
docs.text:
Page Module Suggested form Property pages Property Details › Inquiry form Property inquiry: first name, email, phone, message Sell your home Form Section Home valuation: name, email, phone, address, postal code, home type Contact Contact Section Contact: name, email, phone, "I'm looking to…", message Single agent and commercial homes Form Section Contact (the same form works) New development home Form Section Register interest: name, email, phone

Create the forms in Marketing › Forms, then click the module in the page editor and choose the form. The theme styles every form to match your colors and fonts.

docs.title: Know which property each lead asked about
docs.text:
HubSpot already records the page of every form submission on the contact's timeline. To also save the property on the contact record, so you can use it in lists, workflows and notifications, add a hidden field:

  1. Go to Settings › Properties and create a contact property: label Property of interest, internal name property_of_interest, field type Single-line text.
  2. Open your property inquiry form, add Property of interest, and make it a hidden field.
  3. In the Property Details module, check that Hidden field for the property says property_of_interest. It's already filled in.

The theme fills the hidden field with the property's name and address, for example Classic porch home – 1458 Sanchez Street, Noe Valley, San Francisco.

Lead notifications

Create a workflow that sends the property's agent an email when a contact submits the inquiry form, including the Property of interest value.

docs.title: Book a viewing
docs.text: Each agent can have a meeting_link in the Agents table, for example a HubSpot meetings link. Property pages then show a Book a viewing button that opens the agent's calendar. If the agent has no link, the button uses the Viewing link when the agent has no meeting link setting.

docs.title: More contact properties (optional)
docs.text: The demo forms also use Looking to (buy, sell, rent or invest) and Home type (dropdowns). Create them the same way if you want them in your forms and reports.

docs.title: Header, footer and menus
docs.text: The header and footer are global content: edit them once and they change on every page.

docs.title: Create your menus
docs.text:
1. Go to Content › Website pages, click the gear icon for settings, then Navigation. (Or search "Navigation menus" in HubSpot.)
  2. Create a main menu for the header. Add your pages, and drag pages under others to make dropdowns, for example Buy › Homes for sale, Homes for rent.
  3. Create two smaller menus for the footer columns, for example Properties and Company.

docs.title: Edit the header
docs.text:
Open any Openhouse page, click the header, then Open global content editor.

Setting What it does Logo Your logo, its height and link. Leave the logo empty to use the logo from your brand settings Menu Choose your main menu and how many levels to show Phone number Shows your phone number with a label on wide screens Header button The button on the right, for example Book a valuation Top bar An optional dark bar above the header with an announcement, email and office hours Language switcher Shows a language menu when the page has translations

The header can stay at the top while visitors scroll: turn on Sticky header in theme settings under Header.

docs.title: Edit the footer
docs.text:
The footer has your logo, a short text, social links, menu columns (add as many as you need) and your office details (address, phone, email and opening hours), plus a bottom bar with the copyright text, legal links and a legal notice.

Tip

Use the footer's Legal notice for your broker license number, fair housing statement or listing disclaimer.

docs.title: Set up your listings (HubDB)
docs.text:
Openhouse keeps your properties, agents and neighborhoods in three HubDB tables. HubDB is a spreadsheet-like database built into HubSpot (Content › HubDB). Each row becomes a card on your listings page and, on Content Hub Professional, its own page.

A HubSpot theme can't create tables in your account, so you create them once, with our templates. It takes about 15 minutes.

Table Used for Properties Listings page, property pages, featured homes, similar homes Agents Agents page, agent profile pages, the agent box on each property Neighborhoods Neighborhoods page, area guides, home counts per area

You only need the Properties table to start. Agents and Neighborhoods are optional: without them, type agents and areas into the Agent Cards and Neighborhood Tiles modules instead.

docs.title: Download the templates
docs.text:
Each CSV has the demo content (12 homes, 4 agents, 4 neighborhoods) so you can see everything working, then replace it with your own.

  • openhouse-properties.csv
  • openhouse-agents.csv
  • openhouse-neighborhoods.csv

The demo photos are hosted by Pixtheme for your preview. Replace them with your own photos before you go live.

docs.title: Create a table from a CSV
docs.text:
Repeat these steps for each table. Start with Properties.

  1. Go to Content › HubDB and click Create table.
  2. Enter a Table label (for example Properties) and a Table name (for example properties). You can't change the name after publishing.
  3. In the new table, click Actions › Import, upload the CSV and click Next.
  4. On the Map columns page:
    • Map name to Name and page_path to Page path.
    • For every other CSV column, click Add column and give it the same name as the CSV column, with the type from the tables below.
  5. Finish the import and check the rows.
  6. Click Actions › Manage settings, turn on Enable creation of dynamic pages using row data, and save.
  7. Click Publish.

Use the exact column names

The theme finds your data by column name, so use the names exactly as they appear in the CSV (price, main_image, open_house…). Labels can be anything you like.

docs.title: Properties columns
docs.text: Column Type What it does status Select Options: For sale, For rent, Sold, Under offer, Coming soon. Drives the badge and the Buy/Rent filter property_type Select Options such as House, Apartment, Townhouse, Land, Office, Retail. You can add your own types price Number Shown with your currency settings. Leave empty to show "Price on request" price_suffix Text For example /month for rentals beds, baths, parking, year_built Number Key facts. Empty values are hidden area Number Floor area area_unit Text Optional. Overrides the area unit from theme settings for this home address, city Text Shown under the title and searched by the location filter neighborhood Text Must match the name of a row in your Neighborhoods table, for example Noe Valley location Location Map pin on the property page (see below) summary Text One or two sentences for cards and search engines description Rich text The full description on the property page features Text Separate features with commas: Garden, Fireplace, Garage main_image Image The card photo and first gallery photo photo_2 … photo_6 Image More gallery photos floor_plan Image Floor plan image video_url URL YouTube or Vimeo video tour badge Text Extra badge, for example New or Open house Sat 11–2 open_house Text Open house date and time, shown in a box on the property page featured Boolean Featured homes show first and in "Featured properties" sections agent Text The page path of the agent in your Agents table, for example daniel-reyes

docs.title: Agents columns
docs.text: Column Type What it does role Text For example Senior agent, Noe Valley photo Image Portrait photo, about 5:6 phone, email Text Call and email buttons bio Rich text Profile page text languages, areas Text Shown on the profile page meeting_link URL Your HubSpot meetings link. Powers the Book a viewing button on property pages sort_order Number Lower numbers show first

docs.title: Neighborhoods columns
docs.text: Column Type What it does image Image Tile and guide photo, portrait works best summary Text Short intro description Rich text The full area guide location Location Map on the area guide highlights Text Separate highlights with commas sort_order Number Lower numbers show first

docs.title: Map pins
docs.text: The location column isn't in the CSV files. After the import, add a column named location of type Location, click a cell and search for the address. The map shows on the property page and area guide once a location is set.

docs.title: After the import
docs.text:
Open the table and check:

  • status and property_type show options (not empty cells).
  • featured is ticked for the homes you want to highlight.
  • Images show thumbnails.

If a column came in empty, fill it in directly in the table. Then click Publish.

docs.title: Adding and editing properties
docs.text:
Edit the Properties table like a spreadsheet: click Add row, fill in the cells, then Publish. New rows appear on your listings page and get their own page automatically. The row's Page path is added to your listings page's address, for example /listings/classic-porch-home-noe-valley. Use lowercase words and dashes.

Use the HubSpot CLI instead

Developers can create each table with columns, options and demo rows in one command, using our table definitions: properties, agents, neighborhoods.

hs hubdb create --path openhouse-properties.json

docs.title: Limits
docs.text:
• Filters and sorting run in the visitor's browser on up to 500 properties. That's plenty for most agencies.
  • Next: Build your site.

docs.title: 1. Get the theme
docs.text:
1. Open the HubSpot Template Marketplace and search for Openhouse.
  2. Click Buy and choose your HubSpot account.
  3. HubSpot adds the theme to Content › Design Manager under @marketplace. You don't need to download anything.

docs.title: 2. Set it as your active theme (optional)
docs.text:
If Openhouse will power your whole website:

  1. Open the Themes page in HubSpot (type "Themes" in the HubSpot search bar to find it).
  2. Find Openhouse and click Set as active theme.

docs.title: 3. Set your brand
docs.text:
Before building pages, open Edit theme settings and set:

  • Primary color (buttons, links and highlighted words) and Accent color (badges and small details)
  • Heading font and Body font
  • Under Property listings: your currency, currency position, thousands separator and area unit (sq ft or m²)

See Theme settings for every option.

Note

To open theme settings, edit any Openhouse page, click the Theme icon in the left sidebar of the page editor, then Edit theme settings.

docs.title: 4. Next steps
docs.text:
1. Set up your listings in HubDB. Skip this step on Content Hub Starter.
  2. Build your site.
  3. Connect your forms.

First release.

  • 5 home page designs: agency, single agent, luxury, commercial and new development
  • Property listings with search, filters and sorting, and property pages from HubDB
  • Agents and neighborhoods with profile and guide pages from HubDB
  • Sell your home, About and Contact templates
  • Blog listing and blog post templates
  • 11 system page templates
  • 24 modules plus the site header and footer
  • 12 ready-made sections
  • Section style and Custom styles on every module
  • HubDB CSV templates with demo content

docs.title: FAQ and troubleshooting
docs.text:
My listings page says to choose a table

Click the Property Listings module and choose your table under Properties table. The message only shows in the editor.

Property pages show a 404

Check that the page's Settings › Advanced › Dynamic pages data source is your Properties table, that Enable creation of dynamic pages is on in the table settings, and that the table is published.

The Buy/Rent filter or status badges look wrong

Check the status column is a Select column with the options For sale, For rent, Sold, Under offer and Coming soon, and that every row has a status.

The map doesn't show

Add a location column of type Location to your table and set a location for each row. See Map pins.

Properties don't show their agent

Choose your Agents table in the Property Details module, and make sure the property's agent column has the agent's page path (for example daniel-reyes), not their name.

Prices show the wrong currency

Set Currency, Currency position and Thousands separator in Theme settings › Property listings.

Can I import listings from my MLS?

Openhouse doesn't include an MLS or IDX feed. You can import a CSV into HubDB at any time, or contact us about a custom sync.

Do I need Content Hub Professional?

Only for automatic property, agent and neighborhood pages from HubDB. On Starter, use the typed-in modules. See Content Hub Starter.

docs.title: Support
docs.text:
We're happy to help with setup questions and anything that doesn't work as described.

Email: support@pixtheme.com

Please include:

  • A link to the page with the problem
  • What you expected to happen and what happened instead
  • A screenshot, if it helps

Need more, like an MLS sync, a custom module or a full site build? We also offer HubSpot development services.

Support is in English.

docs.title: All modules
docs.text: Every module has a Content tab and a Style tab (Section style and the Style tab). Labels and button texts can be translated in each module's Labels and translations group.

docs.title: Properties
docs.text: Module What it does Property Listings Properties from HubDB: all homes with search, filters and sorting, featured homes, similar homes, an agent's homes or homes in an area Property Cards Property cards you type in. Works without HubDB Property Details The property page: gallery with lightbox, key facts, description, features, floor plan, video, map, agent box, inquiry form and viewing button Mortgage Calculator Monthly payment from price, down payment, rate and term, with taxes and insurance. Uses the property price on property pages Unit Types Floor plan cards for a new development, with beds, size and price Availability Table Units with floor, size, price and availability status

docs.title: People and places
docs.text: Module What it does Agent Cards Team grid from HubDB or typed in Agent Profile The agent profile page: portrait, bio, languages, areas and contact buttons Neighborhood Tiles Area tiles from HubDB or typed in, with optional home counts Neighborhood Guide The area guide page: description, highlights and map Client Reviews Star ratings and quotes with an overall rating Logo Strip Logos of partners, press or tenants

docs.title: Page building
docs.text: Module What it does Home Hero Hero in 3 layouts, with property search, buttons and trust facts Page Intro Heading and text at the top of inner pages Service Cards Icon cards with links Image and Text Photo with stat card, text, checklist, buttons and stats Process Steps Numbered steps Photo Gallery Grid or mosaic gallery with lightbox FAQ Accordion of questions Call to Action Banner Banner with photo, heading and two buttons Latest Posts Recent posts from your blog

docs.title: Forms
docs.text: Module What it does Form Section Text and checklist next to a HubSpot form Contact Section HubSpot form with office details, opening hours and map

docs.title: Site
docs.text: Module What it does Site Header Logo, menu with dropdowns, phone, button, top bar and language switcher Site Footer Logo, text, social links, menu columns, contact details and legal notice Error Page Content for the 404 and 500 pages

docs.title: Blog
docs.text: Openhouse includes a Blog listing and a Blog post template.

docs.title: Use them for your blog
docs.text:
1. Go to Settings › Content › Blog, choose your blog, and open Templates.
  2. Set Blog listing page to Openhouse Blog listing and Blog post template to Openhouse Blog post.
  3. Save.

docs.title: Blog listing
docs.text:
• On page one, the newest post is shown large, then a grid of cards.
  • Topic buttons at the top filter posts by topic. Topic and author pages use the same template.
  • A newsletter box with your blog subscription form.
  • A banner below the posts. It sits in a drag-and-drop area: edit it in the blog listing editor, swap it for another module, or remove it.

docs.title: Blog post
docs.text:
• Breadcrumb, author, date and reading time.
  • Cover image from the post's featured image.
  • Share buttons (Facebook, LinkedIn, X and copy link) that stay in view while reading.
  • Topics, an author box, comments (when turned on for the blog) and three related posts from the same topic.

Turn each part on or off in Theme settings › Blog.

docs.title: Page templates
docs.text:
Template What's on it Home Hero with property search, featured properties, services, image and text, neighborhoods, agents, client reviews, call to action, latest blog posts Home – single agent Hero, logo strip, the agent's listings, image and text, how it works, client reviews, contact form, latest blog posts Home – luxury Full-screen photo hero, logo strip, curated listings, image and text, photo gallery, neighborhoods, call to action Home – commercial Hero, tenant logos, services, offices and retail spaces, image and text, how it works, leasing contact form, latest blog posts Home – new development Project hero, image and text, amenities, photo gallery, unit types, availability table, register-interest form, FAQ Property listings and property pages Listings with search, filters and sorting; property pages with gallery, key facts, features, floor plan, video, map, agent, inquiry form, mortgage calculator and similar homes Agents and agent profiles Team grid; profile pages with bio, contact buttons and the agent's listings; client reviews and call to action Neighborhoods and neighborhood guides Area tiles; guides with description, highlights, map and homes in the area; call to action Sell your home Valuation form, how selling works, image and text, client reviews, FAQ, call to action About Page intro, image and text, services, team, client reviews, call to action Contact Page intro, contact form with office details and map, FAQ

Every template is built with drag-and-drop areas: move, remove or add modules and sections freely.

Latest blog posts

The Latest Posts section shows posts from your HubSpot blog. If you don't have a blog yet, remove the section from the page.

docs.title: System pages
docs.text:
System pages are the pages HubSpot shows in special situations. Openhouse styles all of them to match your site.

Template Where to choose it 404 Page not found and 500 Server error Settings › Content › Pages › System pages Search results and Password prompt Settings › Content › Pages › System pages Email subscription preferences, Backup unsubscribe, Subscription update confirmation Settings › Marketing › Email › Subscriptions Membership login, register, reset password request and reset password Settings › Content › Private content › Templates

The 404 and 500 pages use the Error Page module: edit its heading, text, search field, buttons and helpful links in the page editor.

docs.title: Welcome to Smart Comparison Table
docs.text:
Smart Comparison Table is a free HubSpot module for comparing pricing plans or products side by side. You fill in simple fields in the page editor, and visitors get a clear table with check and cross icons, tooltips, a "show differences only" switch and layouts made for phones.

Live demo: assets.pixtheme.com/modules/comparison-table-demo

docs.title: What's included
docs.text: Columns 2 to 6 plans or products, each with a name, description, price, badge, optional logo and button Rows Up to 80 feature rows and section headings, with optional tooltips Values yes, no and partial become icons. Any other text, such as 10 GB, shows as text For visitors "Show differences only" switch, a slim sticky bar with the column names on desktop, tooltips On phones Swipe the table with the feature names fixed, or show one card per column Style Light, Dark and Brand tint presets, your brand color, custom colors, row height, stripes, corner radius

docs.title: Where to start
docs.text:
• Install the module
  • Build your table
  • Examples

docs.title: Requirements
docs.text:
• A HubSpot account that can create website pages or landing pages.
  • Any HubSpot theme. The module uses your theme's primary color by default and looks the same in every theme.
  • No coding is needed. Everything is edited in the HubSpot page editor.

docs.title: Examples
docs.text: All three examples are on the live demo page.

docs.title: Pricing plans
docs.text:
• 3 columns with prices, periods and buttons.
  • Highlight this column and a Most popular badge on the plan you recommend.
  • Section headings such as Core features, Collaboration and Support and security.
  • Light preset, with Repeat buttons below the table turned on.

docs.title: Us vs competitors
docs.text:
• Your product in the first column, highlighted, with an Our pick badge and a button. Competitors without buttons.
  • Mostly yes, no and partial values, so differences stand out.
  • Dark preset and One card per column on phones.
  • A footnote with the source and date of the comparison.

Keep competitor comparisons fair

Use public information, add the date in the footnote and update the table when competitors change their plans.

docs.title: Product or platform comparison
docs.text:
• 2 columns with text values such as Handled by HubSpot or You manage it.
  • Tooltips to explain features that need context.
  • Brand tint preset in your own color and a smaller Maximum width.

docs.title: Style settings
docs.text: Open the module's Style tab.

docs.title: Color preset
docs.text: Preset Best for Light White sections on light pages Dark Dark sections and dark themes Brand tint A light tint of your brand color, to make the table stand out from the sections around it

docs.title: Brand color
docs.text: Brand color is used for the highlighted column, badges, buttons, check icons and the switch. It follows your theme's primary color until you choose a different one.

docs.title: Custom colors
docs.text: Override the preset with Background, Text color, Border color, Included icon color and Not included icon color. Leave a color empty to use the preset.

docs.title: Layout
docs.text:
• Row height: comfortable or compact.
  • Striped rows: alternate row backgrounds for easier reading.
  • Corner radius: 0 to 32 px.
  • Maximum width: 600 to 1600 px. Use a smaller width for tables with 2 columns.

Works with any theme

Many themes add their own colors and borders to tables. Smart Comparison Table resets those styles inside the module, so it looks the same in every theme.

docs.title: Table options
docs.text: Open Table options in the module's content settings.

docs.title: Show differences only
docs.text: Show the 'differences only' switch adds a switch above the table. When visitors turn it on, rows that have the same value in every column are hidden, along with section headings that no longer have any rows. Change the switch's text in Switch label.

docs.title: Sticky bar with the column names
docs.text:
Keep column names visible while scrolling shows a slim bar with the column names and prices while visitors scroll through a long table on desktop. It appears after the column headings scroll out of view and hides near the end of the table.

The bar finds your site's fixed or sticky header and sits right below it. If your header has an unusual setup and the bar ends up underneath it, set Sticky header offset to your header's height in pixels. Leave it at 0 for automatic.

docs.title: Mobile layout
docs.text:
Option What visitors see on phones Swipe the table The full table. Visitors swipe sideways, and the feature names stay fixed on the left One card per column Each plan or product as its own card, with all its values listed

Cards work well for 3 or more columns with short feature names. Swiping works well when visitors need to compare columns directly.

docs.title: Buttons and footnote
docs.text:
• Repeat buttons below the table: shows each column's button again at the bottom, so visitors don't have to scroll back up.
  • Footnote: small text below the table, for example tax, trial or data source details.

docs.title: Labels and translations
docs.text: Labels and translations holds text that screen readers announce: the meaning of the icons (Included, Not included, Partly included, Not applicable) and the info button. Translate these for pages in other languages. The First column heading in Table options is also read by screen readers, even when it's hidden.

docs.title: Build your table
docs.text: A new Smart Comparison Table starts with a finished example: three pricing plans with section headings, icons and tooltips. Change the example instead of starting from an empty table.

docs.title: 1. Heading and text
docs.text:
Under Heading and text, set the Eyebrow (small label), Heading and Intro text. Leave any of them empty to hide it.

  • Heading level: use H2 in most cases. Use H1 only if the table is the main heading of the page.
  • Alignment: left or center.

docs.title: 2. Columns
docs.text:
Each column is a plan or a product. Under Columns (plans or products) you can add 2 to 6 columns and drag them to change the order.

Field What it does Name Plan or product name, for example Professional Short description One line under the name Price and Price period For example $49 and /month. Leave the price empty for product comparisons Badge Small label above the name, for example Most popular Highlight this column Adds a border and background in your brand color. Use it for one column Logo Optional logo above the name, shown 32 px high Button Text, link and style (filled or outline). Leave the text empty to hide the button

docs.title: 3. Rows
docs.text:
Under Rows, each row is either a Feature row or a Section heading. Section headings group the rows below them, for example Core features or Support.

For a feature row, fill in:

  • Label: the feature name, for example Storage.
  • Tooltip: optional extra explanation. Visitors see it when they hover, tab to or tap the small i button.
  • Values: one value per column, in the same order as your columns, separated by |.

docs.title: Writing values
docs.text:
You type Visitors see yes Check icon (Included) no Cross icon (Not included) partial Half-filled icon (Partly included) - A dash (Not applicable) Any other text, like 10 GB or 24/7 The text

Example for a table with three columns:

yes | yes | no
3 users | 10 users | Unlimited
Email | Email and chat | Dedicated manager

Type - for an empty cell

Don't leave a value blank in the middle of a row, like yes | | no. HubSpot removes empty values, so the values after it would move one column to the left. Type yes | - | no instead.

Matching is not case sensitive, so Yes and YES work too. ✓, y and true also show a check, and ✗, x and false show a cross.

docs.title: 4. Publish
docs.text: Preview the page on desktop and on a phone, then publish. Next, see the table options and style settings.

docs.title: Install the module
docs.text:
Smart Comparison Table is free on the HubSpot Marketplace.

  1. In HubSpot, click the Marketplace icon in the top navigation and choose HubSpot Marketplace.
  2. Open Templates, then Modules, and search for Smart Comparison Table.
  3. Open the listing and click Install for free. Read the terms, tick the checkbox and confirm.

After installing, the module appears in the page editor's Add panel for website pages and landing pages. Search for "comparison" to find it quickly.

Try it on a draft first

Add the module to a new draft page to explore the settings before you use it on a live page.

docs.title: Updates
docs.text:
Updates from the Marketplace are applied to every page that uses the module. Field names never change between versions, so your content stays as it is.

Next: Build your table.

First release.

  • 2 to 6 columns with name, description, price, badge, highlight, logo and button
  • Feature rows and section headings, with tooltips
  • yes, no and partial icons, plus text values
  • "Show differences only" switch
  • Sticky bar with the column names on desktop, placed below the site header automatically
  • Mobile layouts: swipe with fixed feature names, or one card per column
  • Light, Dark and Brand tint presets, brand color from the theme, custom colors
  • Screen reader labels you can translate

docs.title: FAQ and troubleshooting
docs.text:
Values show up in the wrong column.

A value in the middle of the row is empty, like yes | | no. HubSpot removes empty values, so the rest move left. Type - for an empty cell: yes | - | no.

A row shows a dash at the end.

The row has fewer values than there are columns. Add a value for every column, in column order.

The word 'yes' shows instead of a check icon.

Check the spelling. yes, y, true and ✓ show a check. Text like yes! or yes, with limits shows as text.

The sticky bar sits under my site header.

Set Table options › Sticky header offset to your header's height in pixels. Leave it at 0 to detect the header automatically.

I don't see the sticky bar on my phone.

The bar is for desktop. On phones the table scrolls sideways with the feature names fixed, or shows cards.

The 'Show differences only' switch hides nothing.

Every row has at least one different value, so there's nothing to hide. The switch only hides rows where all columns have the same value.

The table colors don't match my brand.

Set Style › Brand color, or choose another preset. Custom colors in the Style tab override the preset.

Can I use several tables on one page?

Yes. Each table has its own settings.

Which pages does the module work on?

Website pages and landing pages.
